docs.title: Bonds
docs.text:
Bonds is a tool for creating and managing "bonds" between directories using symlinks. A bond is a persistent, bidirectional link between a source directory and a target directory. This allows you to keep your files organized in one place while accessing them from another location.

Bonds provides:

  • A CLI (bonds-cli) for managing symlink-based bonds.
  • A Rust library (bonds-core) for programmatic integration.
# Install the CLI globally
cargo install bonds-cli

# Add bonds-core to your Rust project
cargo add bonds-core

docs.title: Bonds | Architecture
docs.text:
This document provides an overview of the architecture of the Bonds project, including the main components, their interactions, and how they work together to provide the functionality of the tool. The architecture is designed to be modular and extensible, allowing for future enhancements and integrations.

docs.title: High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
A high-level overview of the main components and their relationships. This is intentionally simple to keep it readable on mobile devices. See the detailed sequence diagram below for more specifics on interactions.

    user["User / Shell"] --> cli["bonds-cli"]
    cli -->|invokes| core["bonds-core"]
    core -->|reads/writes| storage["Persistence + OS"]

    %% Optional direct CLI reads (for defaults/config UX).
    cli -->|reads defaults| storage

docs.title: Config Management
docs.text:
Config management is a core concern but is kept separate from the main architecture graph to avoid clutter. The BondsConfig component handles reading/writing the config file and resolving defaults, which is used by both the CLI and core components.

flowchart TB
    %% Keep config concerns separate so the main architecture graph stays uncluttered.
    cfg_cmd["bond config get/set"] --> cfg["BondsConfig"]
    add_cmd["bond add (without target)"] --> cfg
    cfg --> toml["~/.bonds/config.toml"]
    cfg --> def["default_target"]
    def --> resolved["resolved target path"]

    classDef core fill:#34B27B22,stroke:#34B27B,stroke-width:1.8px,color:#34B27B;
    classDef data fill:#E09A3E22,stroke:#E09A3E,stroke-width:1.8px,color:#E09A3E;

    class cfg core
    class toml,def,resolved data

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• bond
  • add
  • list
  • info
  • remove
  • update
  • migrate
  • config
  • metadata
Command Args Description Example(s) bond Main entry point, shows help if no subcommand is provided. 
bond
bond --help
add <source> [--name <name>] Create a bond (symlink) from source to target. 
bond add ~/projects/my-app
bond add ~/projects/my-app --name foo
list List all bonds. 
bond list
info <name|id> Show details about a specific bond. 
bond info foo
remove <name|id> [--with-target] Remove a bond, with optional target deletion. 
bond remove foo
update <name|id> [--source <new-source>] [--target <new-target>] Update a bond's source and/or target. 
bond update foo --source ~/projects/new-app
bond update foo --target ~/bonds/new-app
migrate <name|id> [new-target] Move existing bonds to a new target location (with auto-backup). Moves to the default target if none is provided. 
bond migrate foo
bond migrate foo ~/new-bonds
config <get|set> <key> Get or set configuration values. 
bond config set default ~/my-bonds
bond config get default
metadata <get|set|remove> <name|id> [key] [value] Read or modify metadata for a bond. 
bond metadata get foo
bond metadata set foo project my-app
bond metadata get foo project
bond metadata remove foo project

docs.title: Bonds | Roadmap
docs.text:
• ✔ Phase 1: CLI (core tool)
  • ◌ Phase 2: Library API
  • ✘ Phase 3: GUI Application
  • ✘ Phase 4: Ecosystem & Plugins

docs.title: Phase 1: CLI (core tool) ✔
docs.text:
The primary, usable product. Everything in this phase should work from the terminal.

  • ✔ Create a bond (source -> target symlink)
  • ✔ List bonds
  • ✔ Inspect bond details + health
  • ✔ Remove a bond (with optional target deletion)
  • ✔ SQLite persistence (~/.bonds/bonds.db)
  • ✔ Default target directory (e.g., ~/bonds)
  • ✔ Configurable default directory (bond config set default <path>)
  • ✔ Bulk bonding (bond add ~/projects/ ~/bonds --contents)
  • ✔ Update / rename existing bonds
  • ✔ bond migrate: move existing bonds to a new default location (with auto-backup)
  • ✔ Name a bond (for easier reference and management) (displays in bond list)
  • ✔ Tests for all functionality

docs.title: Phase 2: Library API ◌
docs.text:
Expose bonds-core & bonds-cli as a proper public API so developers can integrate it.

  • ✔ Stabilize and document the public API surface
  • ✔ Add metadata read/write operations
  • ✘ Hooks/events system (bond created, deleted, broken, etc.)
  • ✘ Query bonds by source, target, or metadata
  • ✘ API documentation + usage examples

docs.title: Phase 3: GUI Application ✘
docs.text:
Tauri-based desktop app, depends on Phase 2's API.

  • ✘ Scaffold crates/app (Tauri)
  • ✘ Bond viewer (sorted by recently updated)
  • ✘ Search/filter bonds by source, target, or metadata
  • ✘ Empty-state CTA to create first bond
  • ✘ Open bonded directory from UI
  • ✘ Create / edit / delete bonds from UI
  • ✘ Sidebar bookmarks/favorites
  • ✘ Bond detail panel (source, target, metadata)
  • ✘ Bond relationship visualization (graph view)

docs.title: Phase 4: Ecosystem & Plugins ✘
docs.text:
Long-term extensibility goals.

  • ✘ Plugin interface/framework definition
  • ✘ Editor plugins (VSCode, etc.)
  • ✘ Integration examples for external applications

docs.title: Library API Overview
docs.text:
bonds-core exposes the main primitives:

  • Bond
  • BondManager
  • BondError
  • BondsConfig

The generated Rust API docs are available under /api/bonds_core/. This guide focuses on concepts, workflows, and integration patterns.
